name: Black Sigatoka
description: A devastating fungal leaf disease that affects plantains and bananas. It causes dark streaks and spots on leaves, leading to premature leaf death, reduced fruit fill, and significant yield losses across West Africa.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown spots on lower leaf surfaces
Spots enlarging into dark brown or black streaks with yellow halos
Streaks coalescing into large necrotic lesions
Leaves turning yellow and dying prematurely
Bunches failing to fill properly, small and lightweight fruits
causes: Prolonged leaf wetness from rain or dew
Continuous plantain cultivation in same area
treatments: Apply systemic fungicides (triazoles, strobilurins) at early infection stage
Remove and destroy severely infected old leaves regularly
Spray protectant fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) during rainy season
Alternate fungicide classes to prevent resistance
prevention: Plant disease-free tissue culture plantain suckers
Remove old and diseased leaves during regular field sanitation
Maintain proper plant spacing for air circulation
Use resistant varieties where available (e.g., FHIA hybrids)
Drain excess water from fields to reduce humidity
